LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation, part of Strand 9 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we punctuate written work? 2.How do we use these punctuation marks: comma and full stop?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use commas and question marks correctly to write well punctuated sentences,

2. draw the comma and question marks on cards and display them in the classroom,

3. use punctuation cards to arrange or make coherent sentences and paragraphs featuring the comma and question marks in pairs,

4. make stickers with correctly punctuated sentences and display them at a central place for everyone to see,

5. type sentences on a word processor, tablet or mobile phone and send the work to the teacher or friends,

6. play games such as punctuation ladder and punctuation posters. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use commas and question marks correctly to write well punctuated sentences,
2. draw the comma and question marks on cards and display them in the classroom,
3. use punctuation cards to arrange or make coherent sentences and paragraphs featuring the comma and question marks in pairs,
4. make stickers with correctly punctuated sentences and display them at a central place for everyone to see,
5. type sentences on a word processor, tablet or mobile phone and send the work to the teacher or friends,
6. play games such as punctuation ladder and punctuation posters. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner plays punctuation games and punctuates sentences.

• Digital Literacy: It is enhanced as the learner uses digital devices to type sentences and text, as well as access and play

online and offline games.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is encouraged as the learner engages in assigned roles of typing sentences, making stickers and

drawing commas and question marks to display in the classroom.

• Love: It is nurtured as the learner displays trustworthiness by portraying a caring attitude when appreciating peers’ work

displayed in the classroom.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Personal Safety and Security Education: These aspects are learnt as the learner is taught HIV prevention and the need for

balanced meals for those suffering from AIDs.

• Assertiveness: This is enhanced as the learner understands mechanics of proper punctuation in writing which boosts their

self-esteem for self-expression.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the skill of proper punctuation and in particular the use of the comma and question mark to all other

learning areas as they write essays and other written assignments.
